Born: December 30, 1984, 4:04 PM local time, Akron, Ohio, USA. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating AA.

The AA rating means the time comes from a birth certificate or an equally solid record, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be read at face value. Open LeBron James's chart on Astrolas to follow along.

One part of the chart carries more weight than any single sign or aspect: three planets, Mercury, Saturn and Uranus, all land in the 6th house, the house the Astrolas library ties to daily work, routine and the body. Nothing in a chart explains a jump shot, but a stacked 6th house is a fitting signature for a player whose career has run far past the point where most bodies in his sport give out.

muc.ten: Mercury, Saturn and Uranus together in the 6th house
doan: Mercury sits at 17°05' Sagittarius, Uranus at 15°18' Sagittarius, and Saturn a sign over at 24°37' Scorpio. All three land in the 6th house. Mercury and Uranus sit close enough to form a conjunction, orb 1°47'.

The library reads Mercury in Sagittarius as a quick, restless mind that would rather grasp the big picture than sit with small print, blunt and direct in how it speaks, with a lifelong appetite for new knowledge. Paired with the 6th house, that becomes a need for work that keeps the mind engaged, with a strong pull toward health and daily optimization. Saturn in Scorpio brings enduring resilience, sharp concentration and a real thirst for mastery, while the 6th house turns that into someone who puts duty ahead of rest and quietly takes on work nobody assigned. Uranus in Sagittarius adds an appetite for new methods and a near-restless need to modernize whatever routine it touches, which the library also flags as a generational marker tied to shifts in education and travel for everyone born in this stretch of years.

Mercury conjunct Uranus, in the library's reading, is a breakthrough aspect: original, sharp ideas that sometimes verge on genius, a communication style people remember, and a mind that needs a stable anchor to avoid scattering. Put together, the 6th-house group describes someone who treats the daily, unglamorous side of the job, training, recovery, routine, as the actual craft. James has built one of the most studied and widely reported conditioning routines in his sport, a large part of why he has stayed near the top of his game for far longer than most careers in it last.

muc.ten: Sun, Jupiter and Neptune together in Capricorn
doan: The Sun sits at 9°22' Capricorn and Neptune at 1°27' Capricorn, both in the 7th house, the house the library ties to marriage and close partnership. Jupiter sits one house further on, at 21°12' Capricorn in the 8th.

The library reads Sun in Capricorn as disciplined, patient and quietly ambitious, someone who matures early and climbs toward a goal step by step rather than in one leap, building a reputation over years rather than claiming one overnight. In the 7th house, that drive gets tied to another person: the library says people with this placement build much of their self-worth through a close partnership, and often find real stability and status through a long relationship. James has been with his wife, Savannah, since the two met in high school, long before either of them was famous, a rare thing to see hold across an entire career played in public.

Jupiter in Capricorn, in the library's reading, favors slow, cautious, realistic ambition over any quick win, the kind of growth that looks unremarkable year to year and only becomes obvious looking back; in the 8th house that extends to shared resources, with financial opportunity tending to arrive through partnership rather than alone. Neptune in Capricorn is a generational placement, shared by everyone born in roughly the same stretch of years, but it still softens the Capricorn discipline here with an idealistic, almost old-fashioned view of commitment, a note that sits easily next to James's long list of ventures built off the court in media and business, assembled patiently well after his playing career was already made.

muc.ten: Mars conjunct the Midheaven in Pisces
doan: Mars sits at 4°17' Pisces in the 10th house, close enough to the Midheaven (1°58' Pisces) to form a conjunction, orb 2°19'. The Midheaven marks the most public point of the chart, the career and reputation axis, so a planet sitting this close to it tends to describe how a person is seen at work.

The library reads Mars in Pisces as action channeled through feeling and imagination rather than blunt force, a sensitivity to the people and mood around it, with real compassion and a willingness to put in effort for a collective goal rather than only a personal one. In the 10th house, the library's Mars wants to decide every step of the climb for itself and pairs decisive problem-solving with practical thinking, the kind of placement that reaches a high position but needs patience to avoid friction with whoever is technically in charge.

Mars conjunct the Midheaven sharpens that further: the library reads it as drive aimed squarely at career advancement, sometimes to the point of clashing with people above you, plus a real craving to be your own boss. James entered the league straight out of high school and has changed teams more than once since, each move widely covered as his own decision rather than one made for him, a public career built on taking charge of the next step himself.

muc.ten: Moon in Aries in the 11th house
doan: The Moon sits at 16°24' Aries, in the 11th house of friendship and group belonging.

The library reads the Aries Moon as lively, optimistic and quick to show what it feels, generous with time and energy once it cares about someone, but sharply sensitive to being underestimated or dismissed, with a strong reaction when that happens. It adds that this Moon works best under pressure, with a fast, decisive response when something needs handling right away. In the 11th house, the library says close friends get treated as family, often inside groups or organizations where the person naturally ends up in a leadership role, and that goals can shift with mood but rarely stay unfocused once real passion is behind them.

That combination, a Moon that leads through feeling and a house built around group belonging, fits a player whose public identity has always run through his team and, beyond basketball, through steady investment in his hometown of Akron, where he has put money and attention into local education and community programs for years.

muc.ten: Pluto in Scorpio in the 5th house
doan: Pluto sits at 4°20' Scorpio, in the 5th house of creativity, romance and children. Pluto in Scorpio is a generational placement, shared by everyone born between 1983 and 1995, so the sign itself describes a cohort rather than James alone. What makes it personal here is the house: the library reads Pluto in the 5th as love held with total intensity, protection offered to the people closest to you as something close to a duty, and creative projects fed by that same emotional depth. The lesson it names is learning to loosen the grip of control before it turns into pressure on a partner or a child.

James is a father of three, and his oldest son followed him into basketball closely enough that the two have played together as professional teammates, an unusually direct echo of a Pluto placement built around intensity passed down rather than let go of.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: Three planets stacked in the 6th house of routine and upkeep, a Capricorn-heavy 7th and 8th house built around patient partnership, and a Mars sitting right on the career point: none of it explains a single possession, but together it draws a picture of someone whose public story has always been about sustained effort rather than one burst of talent. The Moon in Aries adds the fire and the following that comes with leading a group; Pluto in the 5th adds the intensity that keeps showing up in how he treats the people closest to him.

His Sun is at 9°22' Capricorn, in the 7th house alongside Neptune. His Moon is at 16°24' Aries, in the 11th house of friends and groups.

Three planets together in the 6th house: Mercury, Saturn and Uranus, the house the Astrolas library ties to daily work, routine and the body. It's a fitting match for a player known as much as anyone in his sport for the work that happens off the court.
